narration: Modern question-led explanation of the published memoirs; mature Doubao synthetic voice at native tempo.

historical.work: 1784 torsion and elasticity memoir, MIT translation by Louis L. Bucciarelli, 2000
historical.supports: Prior magnetic-needle suspensions; systematic length, diameter, tension and elastic-restoring studies; oscillatory calibration
Opening fluid-resistance application, apparatus dimensions/materials, measurements0+36,126+18,567+8.5, original576 rounding, zero uncertainty and leakage
Earth-density experiment; related torsion-balance measurement, not a claim of direct replication of Coulomb

analogy.winding_key: Hand-feel analogy only: positive winding and opposing elastic restoring tendency. The key winds forward and holds; the next shot, of the straight silver wire, demonstrates unloading and return. No claim that a clock mainspring bends by the same mechanism as straight-wire torsion, or that Coulomb derived his design from a clock.
analogy.direct_comparison: A faint first equilibrium rod remains while the applied tangential force doubles. Two equal angular intervals make the doubled settled twist directly visible; the force itself is not amplified.

quote_attribution.claim: Measure what is measurable, and make measurable what is not so is widely attributed to Galileo, but lacks reliable primary attribution.

model: Native Full-HD Blender with fine satin silver wire. Same-force comparison of lengths L and 2L, with a midpoint observation mark: each equal half has the same equilibrium relative twist, so the angles add. The lower-rod reference views use matched true-overhead orthographic cameras; upper-driven and lower-driven cases have separate damped ODE trajectories, with equivalent final geometry and relative twist only. Spoken component names trigger gentle highlights.

data_plot.fit: Main relative graph: unweighted log least squares n=1.919190514, plotted on LINEAR axes. SI geometry-corrected alternative n=1.90687003 remains in details.
data_plot.display: Memoir small-angle comparison: alpha/36 for relative distance, (alpha+beta)/36 for relative force; first reading is 1; retain8.5/36 and575.5/36 in third point
data_plot.absolute_force_in_memoir: Revised MIT translation p4 (MIT2000 p3): 360 degrees at 4 pouce arm requires 1/340 grain-weight; first36 degrees requires1/3400 grain-weight; modern conversion approximately0.15 microN.

force_scale.first_measurement: Revised MIT translation p4: 1/3400 grain-weight, approximately 0.153 microN or 15.6 micrograms weight.
force_scale.zero_uncertainty: Revised MIT translation p6 Fourth Remark, French printed p576: zero uncertain by 2-3 degrees, at most about 1/40000 grain-weight, approximately 13 nN or 1.3 micrograms weight. This is an historical estimate of readable microforce, not a modern certified resolution specification.
force_scale.torsion_sensitivity: 1784 memoir section XIV: restoring torque proportional to angle and diameter^4, inverse to length. Equal tangential force at doubled lever arm doubles torque; equilibrium twist doubles.
force_scale.comparison: A 0.01 g reading increment is an illustrative weighing reference, not a universal specification. It is about 642 times the mass-equivalent of the first force, or about 7547 times the memoir zero-uncertainty equivalent. First measured force and uncertainty are distinct quantities.
